label: BigBuy
terms_note: none found (API is the intended channel)

discovery.auth: Bearer JWT API key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>` from the BigBuy control panel; GET /rest/user/auth/status checks it)

auth: 1. Tenant buys a BigBuy pack that includes API access and copies the API key from the control panel
2. Send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (JWT bearer scheme in the spec)
3. Verify with GET /rest/user/auth/status; check prepaid balance with GET /rest/user/purse

endpoints.notes: returns order id; invoice upload for PENDING INVOICE

reference.limits: Not stated in the OpenAPI document. - Paid BigBuy pack with API entitlement - Prepaid purse funds orders - EU GPSR compliance data available per product

fields.name: api_key
fields.help: BigBuy API key from the control panel (API access is part of BigBuy's paid packs), sent as `Authorization: Bearer` (JWT bearer scheme in the OpenAPI spec). Sandbox keys need base https://api.sandbox.bigbuy.eu, which this server does not switch to.

config_fields.name: iso_code
config_fields.help: Two-letter language for product texts and tracking descriptions (the `isoCode` query parameter, e.g. en); BigBuy defaults to es when unset.

config_fields.name: payment_method
config_fields.help: paymentMethod for create_order: paypal, moneybox (prepaid purse, see GET /rest/user/purse) or bankwire; left out of the body when unset.

me.note: GET /rest/user/auth/status.json answers {code: 200, message} when the key is valid (rate limit 1 request/s).

list_products.note: GET /rest/catalog/productsinformation.json (per-language product texts: [{id, sku, name, description, url, isoCode}]); pages are 0-based (`page`, `pageSize`), `category` is the parentTaxonomy tree id and `query` is not accepted by the endpoint. Rate limit 24 requests/hour. Prices come from GET /rest/catalog/productprices.json and stock from /rest/catalog/productsstockbyhandlingdays.json (not mapped); `url` is the product slug, not an absolute link.

get_product.note: GET /rest/catalog/productinformation/{id}.json: {id, sku, name, description, url, isoCode} (rate limit 1 request/5 s). Wholesale/retail prices are in GET /rest/catalog/product/{id}.json and stock by handling days in GET /rest/catalog/productstockbyhandlingdays/{id}.json (not mapped).

create_order.note: POST /rest/order/create.json submits a real order (201 -> {order_id}) and charges the account (paymentMethod from the payment_method setting: paypal, moneybox or bankwire). `shipping_address` is BigBuy's shippingAddress {firstName, lastName, country (ISO-2), postcode, town, address, phone, email, vatNumber, companyName, comment}; `items` are products [{reference (SKU, e.g. S12435678), quantity}]. `shipping_option` is not sent: BigBuy's carriers[{name}] list cannot be built from a string, so the platform picks the carrier. Simulate first with POST /rest/order/check.json (not mapped).

get_order.note: GET /rest/order/{orderId}.json: {id, internalReference, dateAdd, totalPaidTaxIncl, totalPaidTaxExcl, totalShippingTaxIncl, status, carriers[{id, name, price}], shippingAddress, products[{id, reference, quantity, name, priceTaxIncl}]}. Amounts are EUR; tracking numbers come from the track tool.

track.note: GET /rest/tracking/order/{idOrder}.json returns [{id, reference, trackings[{trackingNumber, statusDescription, statusDate, carrier{id}, descriptionTranslated}]}]; the events are the trackings of the first (only) order element. Answers 404 while no tracking exists yet.

not_offered.quote_shipping: POST /rest/shipping/orders.json takes nested order{products[{reference, quantity}], delivery{isoCountry, postCode}} and POST /rest/shipping/lowest-shipping-cost-by-country.json answers a single {reference, cost, carrierId, carrierName} object rather than an options list; neither fits the vocabulary's product_id/country/quantity -> options[] shape.

evidence: host api.bigbuy.eu: DNS ok, TLSv1.2 (Let's Encrypt)
probe: 6/6 tools answered on their documented path with an auth refusal, a validation error or data; control route -> 400 (client_error), so the answers are path-specific
HTML docs spot-check (render-doc): 0/6 tool paths found verbatim on their docs pages, 3 by their last segments; every parameter and body key named on the page
